title: Polymath: Self-Improving Hierarchical Workflow for Multi-Domain Problem Solving
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Physical Design

publication.venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Physical Design

mechanism.populationDetail: The code-workflow evolutionary component is built on OpenEvolve and explicitly uses MAP-Elites with island-based populations; task-flow graph optimization is a separate hierarchical operation.
mechanism.archiveDetail: MAP-Elites maintains diverse high-quality workflow candidates in a program database; evolving candidates are stored for later reuse.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Workflow evolution uses OpenEvolve MAP-Elites/islands; graph nodes are separately merged/decomposed by a multilevel V-cycle.
mechanism.generationDetail: Task graphs are coarsened by merging adjacent nodes and relaxed by LLM-proposed decomposition; code workflows are generated/refined from prior workflow examples and feedback.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A dynamic task-flow graph is optimized via historical surrogate scores and multilevel coarsen/relax operations, alongside a code-workflow EA.

provenance.citationWarning: Island/MAP-Elites and archive labels apply to code-workflow evolution, not to the task-flow graph; exact operator parent count remains retrieval/context-based rather than formal crossover.
